name: Shelomith
bio: Shelomith is the daughter of Dibri, of the tribe of Dan. Her son, whose father was an Egyptian, got into a fight with an Israelite man in the camp and blasphemed and cursed the name of the LORD; he was brought before Moses and held in custody until the LORD's will could be made known. God instructed that he be taken outside the camp, that all who heard him lay their hands on his head, and that the whole congregation stone him (Leviticus 24:10-16, 23). Scripture specifically records Shelomith's name and lineage, while her son is referred to only as "the Israelitish woman's son" and never given a name of his own — making Shelomith the only named individual in Scripture's earliest recorded case of blasphemy punished by execution.
